explanation: The Caspian is a vast lake with no outlet, so the Volga's water never reaches the ocean: it evaporates from the Caspian instead.

claims.text: The Volga River flows into the Caspian Sea.
The Volga does not flow into the Black Sea, the Baltic Sea or the Sea of Azov.
The Caspian Sea has no natural outlet to the ocean.
Water leaves the Caspian Sea mainly by evaporation.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: content:check reports no errors or warnings for this item. Claims: every checkable statement is listed; all standard; I kept 'Europe's longest river' out of the stem so no superlative needs a source. Datasets: natural-earth ne_50m_rivers_lake_centerlines: the Volga's last segment ends at about 46.1° N, 48.7° E, on the Caspian shore near Astrakhan. Rival test: the Black Sea is the main pull (most big Russian and Ukrainian rivers seem to head there), and the Sea of Azov is a strong lure because the Don, which comes close to the Volga at Volgograd, flows into it; the Baltic is the third. Against the key: none. Volatility: evergreen, settled geography with no review date; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: the Volga is famous worldwide; the answer needs map sense, not local schooling. Style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, straight quotes, explanation of 23 words. Myths: every claim screened against content/reference/myths.json; no match. Mystery and encore: nothing of either kind to check in a practice item. Doubts: calling the Caspian 'a lake' in the explanation follows physical geography; its legal status is a separate matter that the item never touches.

evidence.restatement: The Volga ends in a delta on the Caspian Sea near Astrakhan.
The Volga reaches neither the Black Sea, the Baltic nor the Sea of Azov; it ends in the Caspian.
The Caspian is an endorheic basin with no natural outlet to the ocean.
The Caspian loses its inflow mainly through evaporation.
The Volga flows into the Caspian Sea through a delta near Astrakhan.
The Volga does not flow into the Black Sea, the Baltic Sea or the Sea of Azov.
The Caspian Sea is an enclosed basin with no natural outlet to the ocean.
Evaporation removes most of the water the Caspian loses.

issues.note: The explanation says the Volga's water 'never reaches the ocean'. The natural flow does not, but the Volga-Don and other canals move a little Volga water into other basins. 'Cannot reach the ocean by river' or 'the river never reaches the ocean' would be literally safer. No change needed.

editor.reason: Both checks pass with every claim confirmed at certain; every claim is standard risk, so knowledge suffices (§9.5.3). Lint clean, no myth hits. B's canal note concerns engineered transfers; the explanation describes the river's natural flow, so no change.

stem: Into which body of water does Russia's Volga River flow?
